column2: In skin-aging research, it is described as a growth factor involved in fibroblast activity and the production of a skin structural protein (fibronectin).
Research on cosmetics that apply growth factors to the skin is ongoing, but the level of evidence has been assessed as still moderate (Fabi & Sundaram, 2014).
Panthenol
A precursor of vitamin B5 (provitamin B5).

An ingredient widely studied for moisturization and the skin barrier. A review summarizes its moisturizing and barrier-improving effects, including a study in which applying panthenol cream twice daily for 7 days to irritated skin improved skin hydration and barrier function indicators.
Proksch E et al., Journal of Dermatological Treatment, 2017
This product's brightening functional ingredient
A form of vitamin B3.

Its mechanism of reducing the transfer of melanin to the skin's surface cells has been identified, and in a human study with a 5% niacinamide moisturizer, pigmentation decreased and skin became brighter within 4 weeks.
Hakozaki T et al., British Journal of Dermatology, 2002
Madonna lily flower extract
An extract from the flowers of the white lily (Madonna lily), the ingredient behind the product name ‘Backhap’ (Korean for white lily).

The flower has long been used in folk remedies and cosmetics in many regions, and several plant compounds in it, such as kaempferol, are known for their antioxidant activity. This product contains 0.001 ppm as an ingredient that symbolizes its name.
Zaccai M et al., Plants, 2020

The ‘What research shows’ notes below summarize research on each raw material. They are not tests of NEUVELIF products, and most of the research used leave-on products or other forms. This product is a rinse-off cleanser, so ingredients stay on the skin only briefly.
Matcha-derived PDRN (sodium DNA)
DNA fragments (polydeoxyribonucleotide) obtained from matcha. Contains 0.01 ppm.
Most PDRN research involves salmon-derived PDRN used as injections. Reviews note that research on applying plant-derived PDRN to the skin is still at an early stage.
Review of plant-derived PN/PDRN, Journal of Functional Biomaterials, 2026
Caffeine
An ingredient found in coffee and tea, known to penetrate the skin well.
It is widely used in cosmetics because of research on microcirculation and antioxidant activity, though many of these studies are reportedly cell or animal studies.
Escin
A saponin obtained from the seeds of the horse chestnut (marronnier).

Studies in which people with weak leg venous circulation took horse chestnut seed extract (main component: escin) as capsules are summarized as showing reduced leg swelling. These were not studies of leave-on or rinse-off products.
Low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid
A broken-down form of a classic moisturizing ingredient that holds water in the skin.
In a study applying 0.1% hyaluronic acid cream for 60 days, skin hydration and elasticity improved, and smaller molecules are described as penetrating the skin better.
Pavicic T et al., Journal of Drugs in Dermatology, 2011
Ceramide NP
A lipid that fills the spaces in the skin's stratum corneum.
Ceramides are epidermal lipids important to skin barrier function and are described as being used in skincare products to replenish them.
